root.name: Vienna Gambit, with Max Lange Defense

overview: White offers the f-pawn with 3.f4 exf4 and aims for rapid development with Nf3, d4 or Bc4 against f7, together with kingside castling and a central pawn centre. Black, whose knight is not on f6, can take the pawn without e4-e5 hitting a knight, and usually plays ...g5 or ...d5 to hold it or give it back. The play is open and tactical, and equality is generally accepted with accurate play.

white_ideas.idea: Regain the pawn with d4 or Nf3 and Bxf4, building a big centre
Develop quickly with Nf3, Bc4 and O-O, aiming at f7
Use the open f-file and a kingside attack if Black over-extends with ...g5

black_ideas.idea: Accept with 3...exf4 and hold the pawn with ...g5 or ...Bc5
Strike back with ...d5 and return the pawn for equality
Develop ...Nf6, ...Bc5 and castle short, then use the extra pawn in an endgame

typical_structures.structure: Open centre after d4 and Bxf4 or ...d5 exd5, with open f- and e-files

character.notes: White gives a pawn for the initiative and Black can lose quickly to attacks on f7 and the open king; both sides take risks.

gambit.notes: After 3...exf4 Black can keep the pawn with ...g5 or ...d5, so it is a real gambit. The root itself is just 3.f4, before it is taken.

soundness.notes: Sound at the level of equality; strong players accept it as playable.

structure.notes: Central pawns come off early; open e- and f-files and diagonals for the pieces.

approach.notes: A respectable if less common gambit against 2...Nc6, played by strong players now and then.

level.notes: Needs knowledge of the 3...exf4 4.Nf3 g5 lines with Nxg5 and h4 sacrifices; the ideas are clear but the theory bites.

sublines_that_differ.name: 4.Nf3 g5 5.h4 pawn-storm line
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nc3 Nc6 3. f4 exf4 4. Nf3 g5 5. h4 g4 6. Ng5
sublines_that_differ.how: Very sharp with knight sacrifices on f7 and mutual attacks.

sublines_that_differ.name: Declined with ...d6
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. e4 e5 2. Nc3 Nc6 3. f4 d6
sublines_that_differ.how: Black does not take; no material is offered and the game is quieter.

character.reason: A pawn sacrificed for the initiative with open lines and tactics.

gambit.reason: White offers the f-pawn, which Black can keep.

soundness.reason: Equal with accurate play; not considered refuted.

structure.reason: Open e- and f-files and diagonals with centre pawns exchanged.

approach.reason: Less common but played by strong players, not a rare surprise.

level.reason: Memorisation of the sharp lines matters but the main ideas are accessible.

plans.reason: White regains the pawn with development and targets f7.
